question: A store sells a printer priced at ₹32,000, offering a trade discount of 9%. What is the discount amount?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The discount amount can be directly calculated as a straight percentage of the marked price.

Discount = 9% of 32000

Discount = (9 ÷ 100) × 32000

Discount = 9 × 320 = 2880

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,880.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (Price of printer) = ₹32,000

Trade Discount percentage = 9%

**Formula Used:**

Discount Amount = Marked Price × (Discount Percentage ÷ 100)

 
 Marked Price (MP)
 ₹32,000
 
 
• 
 

 9% Discount
 
 
 Discount Amount
 ₹2,880
 
 Discount = 9% of ₹32,000 = ₹2,880

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount Amount = 32000 × (9 ÷ 100)

⇒ Discount Amount = 320 × 9

⇒ Discount Amount = 2880

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,880.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Selling Price (SP)

Selling Price is the final amount at which the item is sold after deducting the discount. Formula: SP = Marked Price − Discount.

Successive Discounts

When two discounts of a% and b% are given successively, the equivalent single discount can be calculated using the formula: [a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)]%.

Trade Discount

A trade discount is a direct percentage reduction in the listed price (marked price) of an item, commonly provided by a manufacturer or wholesaler to a retailer.
